column1: # These rank above all 148k unicode names, so a keyword here wins the query.
# That is the point: `heart` should land on the heart Astrid actually uses
# (U+2661 WHITE HEART SUIT) rather than on SPARKLING HEART.
# This file is both its own tab-menu and the boost list for the `dotkey` tab.
# Every *.tsv beside it in this directory gets the same treatment, so a new
# set of glyphs is a new file, not a patch to this one.
# five scripts that each echoed one glyph into an xclip that then had to stay
# resident forever to own the selection. An xclip still lingers -- X11 has no
# clipboard storage, so the owner has to stay alive to serve the bytes -- but
# there is one of them for every glyph rather than five scripts' worth, and the
# Multi-character entries are fine; kaomoji are the whole reason.
# Edits are live on the next popup; a brand new .tsv needs commando --restart.
